name: TimeTree
tagline: A shared calendar app for families, couples and small groups, with per-event chat and mobile apps.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not hard: shared calendars, events, invitees, comments on events, a month view and an agenda view. An agent can produce a self-hosted shared calendar with invite links and event threads in a weekend, and for a household of two to four people that is genuinely enough. What breaks is everything around the edges: polished native apps with home screen widgets, notifications that actually arrive, two-way sync with Google and Apple calendars, and offline editing on a phone in a parking garage. The other half of the problem is social, since a shared calendar is only useful if the people you share your life with agree to open it. Build it if you enjoy the ops; do not expect the rest of the family to be impressed.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted web app where a small group joins a shared calendar by invite code and creates, edits and comments on events across month and agenda views, with an ICS feed so phones can subscribe read-only.
requirements: A small always-on host or VPS with HTTPS so phones can reach it
Everyone in the group willing to use a web app or PWA instead of a native app
A push provider or ICS subscription as the notification fallback
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps, widgets and share sheet entry points
Push notifications that reliably land, including reminders when the app is closed
Two-way sync with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook, not just a read-only ICS feed
Offline creation and editing with conflict resolution when two people edit the same event
The fact that the people you share a calendar with may already have it installed
moatNotes: The moat is not technical so much as household political: the app has to be on everyone's phone, and switching means renegotiating that with your partner.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a shared calendar is infrastructure for a household, and infrastructure has to be boring and reliable. People pay so reminders fire, so the app opens fast when someone is standing in a school hallway, and so the other adult in the house does not have to be convinced to install a homemade web app. The free tier already covers most families, which means the paid tier is mostly buying ad removal and convenience rather than capability, and that is a low bar to clear compared to running your own server for the rest of your life.
notes: The build is easy, the adoption is not: a family calendar with one user is a diary.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted shared calendar web app for a small group, like a stripped down TimeTree.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/app.db, schema created on first boot
- Tailwind CSS, no component library
- No external services, no analytics, no telemetry

Data model:
- calendar: id, name, invite_code, created_at
- member: id, calendar_id, display_name, color, join_token
- event: id, calendar_id, title, notes, start_at, end_at, all_day, location, created_by
- comment: id, event_id, member_id, body, created_at

Behavior:
- Landing page: create a calendar (name + your display name) or join one with an invite code.
- Identity is a signed cookie holding member id. No passwords, no email, no OAuth. Invite codes are the only auth boundary; say so plainly in the README.
- Calendar view: month grid as default, plus an agenda list for the next 30 days. Events colored by the member who created them.
- Create and edit events in a side panel, not a separate page. Support all-day and timed events, and a simple daily/weekly/monthly repeat rule.
- Each event has a comment thread. Comments show the member name and relative time.
- Read-only ICS feed per calendar at /api/ics/[invite_code].ics so phones can subscribe in Apple or Google Calendar.
- Add a web app manifest and basic service worker so it installs as a PWA. Do not attempt web push.

Explicitly out of scope: two-way Google or Apple sync, push notifications, file attachments, timezones beyond a single TZ set in .env, native apps.

Deliverables: working app on `npm run dev`, .env.example with SESSION_SECRET and APP_TZ, seed script that creates one calendar with two members and a week of sample events, and a README covering deploy behind HTTPS and how to back up data/app.db.
